questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have a personal connection to the city. Even though that played a part, it was crucial to gain insights away from my home university in order to gain advantages in terms of career opportunities in the future.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You should sugar coat the experience way less. People are mostly nice and there are a lot of academic and cultural insights to gain, but it is also bureaucratically very frustrating and you are alone most of the time. I don't think people generally get friendships that lasts for a lifetime either. It can happen of course and that is good, but mostly I think people should think of it as a task that needs solving more than anything else.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Difficult to say the least

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A meeting that answered non of my questions. Only when I forced my Erasmus-coordinator at the guest University to have a one-on-one sitting with me, did things start to find their shape

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: A crucial comment to make in this regard, is that the above-mentioned coordinator was very helpful and nice

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not super hard just really expensive

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it is expensive

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I do not have an oponion

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The way you register at Humboldt was invented in hell

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You need to just show up and get signed in, but you can never be sure if that is in fact going to happen because everybody needs signing in and there is people everywhere and it is your responsibility to just fix it. You never know which courses you are going to get as an exchange student and all of the courses in my pre-approval was not being taught which ment I had to start from scratch terrified that i wouldn't be able to get the 30 ECTS required and therefore not get my bachelors degree. Just terrible, counterproductive and completely unnecessary.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Nothing really. Even the people who are supposed to help you don't always know what to do or how the rules is applied. This means you have to be extremely proactive in order to get each little tiny thing done which is quite exhausting when you are also trying to study and do so in a new language you are not fluent in.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get any of them. But i got the best out of things anyway. Mostly I was just happy I was able to get my 30 ECTS at all and not to bothered about the subject.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare for war, learn the language to the best of your abilities and expect things to go wrong and be very frustrating and complicated

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They were very good professor's with great knowledge about their subjects

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My co-students seemed quite lazy at the IfEE. This had nothing to do with my professor's they were great and very capable. At philosophy the dedication was very different and the abstraction levels therefore higher. It was super high level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is a higher degree of praxis orientation on UCPH. Most of them haven't even conducted interviews or anything which to me was quite shocking. And they were much lazier and the sense that they seemed, at least to me, ill prepared and unwilling to participate

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: Very, as long as you drink the same amount of beer as the locals you'll be fine

questions.answer: No, except for learning their language. People don't bother speaking english, really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I adore germans. Particularly berliners. Their humor is very dry
